meta.intro: OpenAI says it has settled a 50-year-old math problem, while the companies that buy AI hardware are starting to buy its parts directly.
meta.summary: Across today's stories, AI's margins are moving toward whoever is closest to the scarce input. Google is reportedly buying HBM itself instead of through Broadcom, both HBM makers are funding a microLED alternative to lasers, and Meituan's Keeta replaced a GPT-5.4 support agent with a 31B open model it trained itself. Japan is moving the same way: Sakana is setting up a defense unit that runs only on servers in Japan, JERA wants US AI labs to build data centers at its power plants, and Tokyo may require chip users, not just suppliers, to file sourcing plans. The caveat throughout is that most of these are talks, projections or claims nobody outside the company has checked yet.

gaps.label: Sovereign frontier-model pretraining
gaps.note: Unchanged. Sakana says work on its 'Sawara' foundation model starts this month, with a small on-prem model due in early 2027. Its shipping Namazu line is built on open models, not trained from scratch. Meanwhile, OpenAI and Anthropic are now settling open problems in mathematics.

gaps.label: Depth of private risk capital for AI infrastructure
gaps.note: Unchanged. JERA's talks with Anthropic and Meta are not signed, and both the anchor tenants and much of the capital come from abroad. In the US, Applied Digital signed a 150 MW, $5.4B lease at about $2M per MW per year, and Avicena raised $100M+ before it has a product.

gaps.label: Domestic leading-edge chip manufacturing
gaps.note: Japan down 1. Preferred Networks is having Samsung make its next MN-Core chip rather than Rapidus. Rapidus has given no fix for its slipped 2nm SRAM milestone. A proposed rule requiring chip users to file sourcing plans could create demand, but it is still only being studied. TSMC has filed plans for a $22.6B fab campus in Texas.

gaps.label: Early-stage AI venture formation and exits
gaps.note: Unchanged. No new AI-native VC fund entered Japan this week, and Sakana has ruled out a near-term IPO. In New York, a USV partner's own startup Supertake raised a $20M seed, and Every raised at a $110M valuation, which shows how readily US investors fund AI-native startups.

items.headline: OpenAI Posts a Preprint Claiming Matrix Multiplication's Exponent Is Exactly 9/4, With a Matching Lower Bound, Plus a Fourier Bound Below FFT's
items.dek: Days after the Lean-checked Riemann proof made with Claude, OpenAI says it has settled a question open for over 50 years, but no one outside OpenAI has checked the full proof.

analysis.happening: On Nov 24 OpenAI's openai/math repo paired its October upper bound of 9/4 with a lower bound of at least ⌈n^(9/4)/2⌉ multiplications, which it says holds over every field. A second preprint claims the Fourier transform can be computed in N(log N)^(1/2+o(1)) gates, below the O(N log N) FFT bound.
analysis.now: If this holds, frontier labs are settling foundational open problems in mathematics, not just topping benchmarks. Caveats: the Lean proof covers only division-free circuits, and the result is asymptotic, so GPU kernels won't change. As of Nov 25 nobody outside OpenAI had checked the full proof.
analysis.future: Watch for independent verification and for any cryptography result. Scott Aaronson says he is 'virtually certain' the labs are holding some. Builder angle: tools for Lean formalization and proof checking are becoming core infrastructure, and so are tools that explain machine proofs in plain language.

items.headline: Google Reportedly Buys HBM Itself for TPU v8t, Skipping Broadcom's 15-20% Markup, as Microsoft Picks Intel's EMIB Packaging for Azure Chips
items.dek: Within ten days, two hyperscalers moved to buy parts of their custom chips directly instead of through Broadcom or TSMC.

analysis.happening: Chosun Biz reports Google will buy HBM directly for its MediaTek-built TPU v8t rather than through Broadcom's bundle. Counterpoint puts Broadcom's HBM markup at 15-20%. Bernstein reportedly estimates about $50B in savings, or $8,434 vs $16,996 per TPU. On Nov 18 Microsoft named Intel Foundry's EMIB as packaging for future Azure chips.
analysis.now: The middlemen lose margin, and memory makers, MediaTek and second-source packagers like Intel gain leverage. Caveats: Google hasn't confirmed the HBM move. The $50B figure implies a markup of about 150%; with Counterpoint's numbers it is closer to $16-18B. Microsoft gave no volumes or timing.
analysis.future: Watch for a change in Broadcom's AI guidance, a second named EMIB customer, and SK hynix custom HBM for TPUs. The opening is chiplet and packaging IP, and test tooling, for hyperscalers that now assemble their own chip supply chains.

items.headline: Avicena Raises $100M+ to Replace Lasers With MicroLEDs in Chip-to-Chip Links, With SK hynix, Samsung, AMD and Two Japanese Corporate VCs Investing
items.dek: Both big HBM makers and a GPU vendor are backing a laser-free optical interconnect, which goes against today's consensus on co-packaged optics.

analysis.happening: Korea's InterVest led Avicena's Series C. Tiger Global, Cerberus, SK hynix Ventures, Samsung Catalyst, AMD Ventures, Prosperity7, Diamond Edge (Mitsubishi Chemical) and Hitachi Ventures joined. LightBundle carries data over many slow 4Gbps microLED lanes on multicore fiber. 1Tbps evaluation kits have shipped since August.
analysis.now: The investor list is the signal: memory makers expect copper links between chips and memory to run out. Avicena joins Lumilens ($700M+) and CScale ($145M) in this year's optical rounds. Caveats: there's no commercial product until 2027, no power-per-bit figure has been disclosed, and a new CEO took over at the time of the raise.
analysis.future: Watch for a first design win with an HBM or accelerator maker, and published pJ/bit figures against co-packaged optics. Japan angle: Mitsubishi Chemical and Hitachi now hold stakes, a possible way in for Japanese materials and multicore-fiber packaging suppliers.

items.headline: Meituan's Keeta Replaces a GPT-5.4 Support Agent With a Gemma-4-31B It Retrained Itself, Projecting 70.5% Lower Support Cost per Order
items.dek: A production write-up of a self-improvement loop that let a 31B open-weight model beat a frontier closed model on live customer-service traffic.

analysis.happening: Keeta, Meituan's overseas delivery unit, post-trained Gemma-4-31B-IT into CARE-31B over five rounds. Each round served live traffic, ran a 24-hour inspection, traced each error to its cause, generated repair samples and retrained the model on its own outputs. The bad-case rate fell from 6.42% to 1.97%, against 4.60% for the GPT-5.4 model it replaced. Model-serving cost fell 92.8%.
analysis.now: This is a reusable playbook: in one narrow domain, open weights plus a quality-check loop can replace a frontier API. Caveats: the 70.5% saving is a projection for full replacement, the rollout covers only some regions, early versions underperformed, and the error-tracing step still relies on a stronger closed model.
analysis.future: Opening: agent-ops tooling that packages the inspect, trace, repair and retrain loop for mid-size companies. Japanese call centers and outsourced back-office operators, both labor-constrained and high-volume, are obvious first buyers.

items.headline: New York's Supertake, Started Inside Union Square Ventures, Raises a $20M Seed Led by Adjacent for Agents That Turn Plain-English Market Bets Into Live Portfolios
items.dek: Agentic trading built on top of existing brokers such as Robinhood and Coinbase, without holding customer assets, and backed by New York money.

analysis.happening: USV partner Michael Mignano (co-founder of Anchor) started Supertake inside the firm. Its CEO and CTO come from Coinbase's AI team. It raised $20M after a $2M pre-seed. Adjacent led, with USV, Coinbase Ventures and angels Nat Friedman, Guillermo Rauch and Scott Belsky joining. Agents research a user's bet, build a portfolio and trade it through a linked brokerage. Users can copy others' bets from a leaderboard.
analysis.now: The bet is that agents become the layer users trade through, on top of existing brokers rather than replacing them. Separately, IA Ventures led a $17.5M Series A for New York's Every at $110M. Caveats: Supertake is a waitlist-only beta with no disclosed users, assets or fees, and its regulatory status is unstated.
analysis.future: Watch how the SEC and FINRA treat AI portfolios that users can copy, since copy-trading and advice rules apply. Japan opening: nobody yet runs agents on top of brokerage APIs for NISA accounts.

items.headline: Sakana AI Spins Out 'Sakana Defense': Japanese-National Staff Only, Models Run Only in Japan, Aimed at SDF Command-and-Control AI
items.dek: Japan's most valuable AI startup is setting up a cleared defense unit, the same split US defense-AI companies use. Tokyo has said it wants a Japanese AI layer above any US command system it buys.

analysis.happening: Sakana set up the unit on Nov 27. Co-founder Ren Ito is also its president, and defense head Motoki Sato is moving over. Staff must be Japanese nationals and models must run in Japan, so classified data stays in the country. It targets Ministry of Defense work, including SDF command and control. CEO David Ha says work on the 'Sawara' foundation model starts this month.
analysis.now: Separating cleared defense work from an open research lab is standard practice for US defense-AI firms; in Japan, Sakana is the first startup to do it. Tokyo has evaluated Palantir Maven and Anduril Lattice and wants a Japanese AI layer above them. Caveat: no contract, budget or product has been announced.
analysis.future: Watch FY2027 Ministry of Defense budget lines for command-and-control AI, and whether Sawara is trained from scratch or, like Namazu, adapted from an open model. Gap: there is little security-cleared, Japan-only tooling (labeling, evals, MLOps) for defense suppliers.

items.headline: JERA Is Talking to Anthropic, Meta and Other US Firms About AI Data Centers at Its Tokyo-Area Power Plants, Skipping Japan's Grid Queue
items.dek: Japan's largest power producer wants to supply data centers directly from its plants rather than wait years for grid connections.

analysis.happening: JERA's chief told Nikkei Asia the company is talking with Anthropic, Meta and other US tech firms about data centers next to JERA plants around Tokyo. UK developer RHAELM handles business development. The first site is Chiba, where JERA, Dell and RHAELM signed an MOU in October for a project of roughly $15B. No tenant has signed. Last week JERA said it is weighing an IPO.
analysis.now: This shows the scarce input in Japan is grid connections, not land or chips. Building at thermal plants skips years of waiting. Every named prospect is American, so the anchor demand comes from abroad. Caveat: these are talks only, with no megawatt figure or signed lease.
analysis.future: Watch whether Chiba signs a hyperscaler, and whether NTT Data's reported Osaka deal for Anthropic (up to 500MW, about ¥1T, targeting March 2027) closes first. Openings: power management, cooling and construction services for data centers built at power plants.

items.headline: Tokyo Proposes Using AI by Default Wherever It Matches Human Accuracy, and Opens Work on Who Is Liable When AI Agents Act
items.dek: A new government panel set out five principles for replacing rules that require human visual inspection, and the PM's regulatory-reform council took up physical AI three days later.

analysis.happening: At its first meeting on Nov 24, a new government panel proposed five principles. The lead one says that where AI is shown to match human accuracy and safety, it should be used by default, with humans still accountable. The panel also began work on legal liability and redress for AI agents, targeting June 2027. On Nov 27, PM Takaichi's regulatory-reform council took up physical AI and medical data.
analysis.now: Japan has hundreds of rules requiring a person to look at something, such as pipe and site inspections. Making AI the default turns those into a procurement market. No other G7 country has a stated AI-by-default principle, and Japan may define agent liability before the US does. Caveat: no specific rules or dates have been named.
analysis.future: Watch the panel's Dec 3 meeting and the year-end summary for which inspection rules change first. Openings: certified drone and vision inspection AI for regulated sectors, and insurance or audit products for AI agents.

items.headline: Japan Weighs Requiring Chip Users to File Sourcing Plans, as Preferred Networks' Next MN-Core Chip Goes to Samsung Rather Than Rapidus
items.dek: Japan has subsidised chip supply for years; now it is studying a rule that would push buyers to diversify, while its leading AI-chip startup uses a Korean foundry.

analysis.happening: Nikkei reports the government is studying a rule requiring end-product makers that use semiconductors and advanced components to file plans for stable sourcing that reduce dependence on any one country. An Economic Security Act amendment is being considered for the 2027 Diet session. Separately, PFN's MN-Core L2000 will be made at Samsung Foundry, with tape-out in Q1 2027.
analysis.now: Japan has paid out over ¥2T for Rapidus and up to about $4.1B for TSMC Kumamoto without requiring anyone to buy their chips. A requirement on buyers would be the missing demand lever; the US relies on subsidies and tariffs instead. PFN choosing Samsung, and Rapidus's slipped 2nm SRAM milestone, show why it may be needed. Caveat: the rule is only being studied.
analysis.future: Watch which chip categories are named and whether the plans must disclose Taiwan or China exposure. Opening: supply-chain mapping and multi-sourcing compliance software for Japanese manufacturers.
